chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Muḥammad ibn Khālid al-Barqī, from Abū al-Bakhtarī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that ʿAlī عليه السلام prayed during...

the salat of the eclipse as two rakʿahs with four sajdahs and four rukūʿs: he stood and recited, then bowed; then he raised his head and recited, then bowed; then he stood and did likewise for two rakʿahs; then he performed two sajdahs; then he stood and did the like of what he had done in the first, equal in its recitation, standing, bowing, and prostration.

key_terms.رَكَعَاتٍ: instances of bowing within the prayer structure

ai.seo_question: How is salat al-kusuf performed according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the structure of salat al-kusuf, stating that it consists of two rakʿahs with four rukūʿs and four sajdahs. It details the sequence of standing, recitation, repeated bowing, and prostration, making it a jurisprudential report on the method of performing the eclipse prayer.
